answer: To crush Sybil attacks, agents must register unique operational nodes by committing to cryptographic stake burning via a verifiable cipher puzzle. Rather than relying on identity as a naive fable, the protocol imposes superlinear friction: each successive node burn scales quadratically, O(n^2), where n is the cluster size. Under this steep cost curve, malicious swarms cannot flex like a supple willow; attacker expenditure explodes to ruinous scale.
